answer: A concrete sybil defense requires each new agent to secure a harbor from three already-established peers. Each sponsor locks stake equal to base plus a multiplier on their current open vouches, creating a beacon that signals rising marginal cost. An attacker must therefore assemble three times as many locked positions for every fake identity; those positions cannot be bought in bulk because each sponsor’s next lock rises. Honest agents thereby maintain an oasis of mutually bonded identities whose expansion cost grows superlinearly with farm size.
